# Armada

> Every coding agent you have running, on one screen. A macOS menu bar app for someone running
> many Claude Code, Codex and Grok Build sessions at once: what each session is doing, how full
> its context window is, and how much of each plan is left, read locally from what the agents
> already write to disk.

Released: a Developer ID signed, notarized zip published on GitHub releases, downloadable at
https://armada.mgcrea.io/download, with a licence at https://armada.mgcrea.io/buy. macOS 26 or
later, and macOS only. Not affiliated with Anthropic, OpenAI or xAI.

## What it shows

- Sessions, per account: every live Claude Code session with its title, project, age and state
  (busy, waiting or idle), read from Claude Code's own session registry rather than inferred. A
  waiting session says what it wants. Sorted by what needs you, groupable by project. Codex and
  Grok Build sessions each get a section of their own.
- Context: how full each session's context window is, where it started, how fast it has grown,
  and when it was last compacted.
- Plan limits: the 5-hour and 7-day windows per account, with reset times, a pace line and a
  forecast, and the Grok Build weekly allowance. Claude limits are asked of the account's own
  `claude` in a request that costs no tokens, falling back to the cache on disk, with a badge
  saying which answered and how old the figure is. Grok Build's is asked of your own `grok`, the
  same question its `/usage` asks.
- Projects: the folders you work in, their live sessions, and the tokens spent in each over 7
  days, 30 days and all time, split by model, account and subfolder.
- Transcripts: a Claude Code session's conversation in a window of its own, with thinking and
  tool calls as filters, and Follow to keep the newest turn in view as it lands.
- Accounts: `~/.claude`, every `~/.claude-*` sibling and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`; `~/.codex` and
  `CODEX_HOME`; `~/.grok` and `GROK_HOME`. Add Account opens an agent on a new folder where you
  sign in with its own sign-in.

## What it does

- Starts `claude`, `codex` or `grok` in a chosen folder on a chosen account, in Terminal, iTerm or
  Ghostty, or a Claude Code session as a tab in the project's VS Code window. Armada never owns
  the agent process.
- Forks a session from where it stands, through each vendor's own fork command. The original is
  left alone.
- Continues a Claude Code session on another account, for one stopped at a limit. The
  conversation is copied to that account and opened there; the original keeps running.
- Closes a Claude Code session the way quitting it would, asking first if it is mid-turn.
  Recently ended lists a project's last eight closed sessions, to read or resume.
- Copies a session's transcript as plain text, or its id as `claude --resume` or `codex resume`
  takes it.
- Focus brings forward the application a Claude Code session runs in, down to its own tab in VS
  Code. Codex sessions have no Focus, because Codex records no process id on disk.
- Middle and extra mouse buttons can cycle the session list or send a keystroke, one button or
  both thumb buttons together, with the modifier you choose.
- The menu bar glyph fills while a session is working and rings when one wants attention.

## The supervisor

- Off until you turn it on in Settings ▸ Supervisor. Armada then serves an MCP endpoint on
  127.0.0.1 (port 8790 unless changed), answering only a bearer token kept in the Keychain.
- One button opens a Claude Code session with that endpoint attached, its read tools pre-allowed
  and a brief written, so you can ask one session which of the others need you, what any of them
  last said, and how much plan is left. Configure adds Armada to Claude Code, ChatGPT & Codex,
  Cursor or VS Code, keeping a backup of the file it changes.
- Eleven tools. Seven are read-only: what needs me, fleet overview, one session, what a session
  said, plan limits, projects, and wait for a change.
- Four more exist only while Allow writes is on, which it is not by default, and none is
  pre-allowed: start or resume a session in a saved project, close a Claude Code session, bring
  one forward, and message one. Messaging also needs Deliver messages to sessions turned on.
- Voice, off by default: press a shortcut anywhere and ask about your sessions out loud. Speech
  is recognised on the Mac, the question goes to Anthropic as text through your own `claude`, and
  the answer is spoken.

## Not built yet

- Messaging between agents across vendors: a supervisor can message Claude Code sessions only.
- Codex and Grok Build folders are not scanned for: a second one is found only when made with
  Add Account. Claude Code's `~/.claude-*` folders are found on their own, without a relaunch.
- New Session needs a terminal that runs a script it is handed, such as Terminal, iTerm or
  Ghostty.

## Privacy and security

- Armada reaches no network on its own, with two exceptions, both off until you act. The update
  check reads one file, armada.mgcrea.io/appcast.xml, which redirects to the GitHub release, and
  sends no identifier: not your licence key, not a machine id. And a Download button in Settings ▸
  Voice fetches the speech models, Parakeet v3 (about 480 MB) or Kokoro (about 95 MB), from
  huggingface.co.
- The licence key is verified offline, on your Mac, with a signature check. No licence server is
  ever contacted by the app.
- It holds no vendor credentials and never opens Codex's `auth.json`.
- It reads the agents' folders, and writes into Claude Code's in three named places only: the
  "trust this folder" flag in `.claude.json` when you start a session in a saved project, one hook
  in each account's `settings.json` while message delivery is on (removed when you turn it off),
  and a copied transcript when you continue a session on another account. Codex's and Grok
  Build's folders are only read.
- What else it writes: its preferences, usage history and saved projects in
  `~/Library/Application Support/io.mgcrea.armada` (usage history kept 30 days, deletable from
  Settings), and a startup script in its own temporary folder when you start a session.
- `make audit` checks the network claim against every build: every Mach-O swept for URL loading,
  DNS and TLS symbols, with three narrowly named allowances: Sparkle, the speech-model
  downloader, and the supervisor's listener, which must bind 127.0.0.1 and nothing else. The one
  entitlement is the microphone, used only while voice listens.
- Not sandboxed, by design: it has to read other tools' folders.
- The `claude` and `grok` it asks for plan limits, and the `claude` voice asks, talk to their
  vendors over your own sign-in. That is those programs' job, not Armada's.
